 Bigger tax refunds: IRS tax credits claimed by tens of millions of filers worth more in 2027
 Updated: Nov. 09, 2026, 5:43 p.m. 
 | Published: Nov. 09, 2026, 5:00 a.m. 
 Two key tax credits will be worth more in 2027. Shutterstock 
 Set as Google Preferred Source 
 By Leada Gore | lgore@al.com 
 Two of the most widely claimed tax credits will be worth more in 2027.
 Along with the annual tax bracket change, the Internal Revenue Service announced the Child Tax Credit and the Earned Income Tax Credit will be increasing. The changes will go into effect in 2027 for taxes filed in 2028.
 What you need to know 
 What is the Child Tax Credit?
 The CTC is a federal tax benefit that lowers the tax bill for eligible parents and guardians on a dollar-for-dollar basis for each qualifying child. Financial experts liken it to a store coupon – if you owe $3,000 in taxes and have one qualifying child, the credit cuts down what you owe.
 What are rules for claiming CTC?
 The child must be under age 17 at the end of the tax year, must have a Social Security number and must have lived with the claiming parent for more than half the tax year. Income limitations also apply with higher earners receiving a partial credit.
 What’s the current CTC?
 Filers in 2026 can claim up to $2,200 with $1,700 of that being refundable, meaning you can receive that amount back even if you owe no taxes. The refundable portion of CTC is known as the Additional Child Tax Credit.
 How is CTC changing in 2027?
 CTC will increase from $2,200 to $2,300 per child in 2027. The amount of credit that is refundable is also increasing by $100 to $1,800.
 How many people claim CTC?
 More than 46 million tax filers claimed the CTC last year, according to the IRS.
 What is the Earned Income Tax Credit?
 The EITC is a refundable federal tax credit for low to moderate-income working individuals and families. It is claimed by some 24 million tax filers a year. It is fully refundable, meaning it can reduce tax liability to zero and result in a direct refund.
 What are rules for claiming EITC?
 Filers claiming EITC must have income from a job and have income below federal thresholds depending on filing status and number of children. The filer and any qualifying children must have a Social Security number.
 What is current EITC?
 For 2026 filing season, EITC is worth:
 No qualifying children – Up to $685 
 One qualifying child – Up to $4,573 
 Two qualifying children – Up to $7,552 
 Three or more qualifying children - $8,231 
 What is EITC for 2027?
 For 2027 filing season, EITC is worth:
 No qualifying children – Up to $685 
 One qualifying child – Up to $4,573 
 Two qualifying children – Up to $7,552 
 Three or more qualifying children - $8,496 
 What is average EITC?
 Last year, the average EITC filing rebate was $2,894.
 Other tax changes
 There are other credit changes in store for 2027:
 The Adoption Tax Credit will increase from $17,670 to $18,250. Up to $5,280 is refundable. 
 Health flexible spending plan contribution limits will increase to $3,500 in 2027, up $100 from 2026. The carryover maximum will increase by $20 to $700. 
 Annual exclusion for gifts will increase to $20,000 up from $19,000. 
 You can see more tax changes here.
